A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are available and readable, allowing reliable matching despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-network experiments and compression-activated backdoor experiments on CIFAR-10, Tiny-ImageNet, and SQuAD, including results in Sections 6–7 and Appendices D and F.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Phi-2 compression experiments in Tables 8, 10, and 11 and a layer-wise sensitivity analysis in Figure 4.

M1.justification: New Section 7.4 introduces a procedural adaptation for noninvertible downstream maps: estimating minimum-norm perturbations through local linearization and the Jacobian pseudoinverse, using autograd. The original exact construction, backdoor losses, SVD compression, and finite-difference power-iteration algorithm remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic four-class classification, CIFAR-10, Tiny-ImageNet, and SQuAD 1.1 question answering. Phi-2 and compression across additional layers expand model configurations and evaluation procedures without introducing a documented new dataset or task.

E2.justification: The standard-backdoor control defined by Equation 11 remains the comparator for compression-activated attacks, including the new Phi-2 experiments. Existing comparisons are retained in the appendices. Newly discussed prior work, including Tsai and Weng, is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds substantially different evaluation configurations: 32-block Phi-2, pruning at 20–40%, single-layer compression at ranks 1800/1700/1500, and compression of all fc2 layers at ranks 2000/1900/1800. Section 7.4 also introduces a layer-wise Jacobian-based evaluation. Existing RoBERTa and vision protocols remain documented.

E4.justification: Section 7.4 and Figure 4 newly examine whether local perturbation estimates remain informative across Phi-2 layers despite failure of exact invertibility assumptions. Table 11 additionally tests backdoor activation under simultaneous compression of all fc2 layers and exposes its clean-accuracy cost. The earlier synthetic-network and spectral-energy analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state five repetitions and retain the existing appendix means and standard deviations. However, the new Phi-2 Tables 8, 10, and 11 display means without deviations; Tables 10–11 still claim standard deviations in their captions. This changes reporting consistency without establishing any change in run counts.

E6.justification: The matched original detailed results are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial Phi-2 evidence. Table 10 reports ASR increasing from 45.5% at full rank to 86.0% at rank 1500; Table 11 reports 99.5% ASR with 55.0% clean accuracy at rank 2000 across all fc2 layers. Figure 4 adds sensitivity findings. These are new settings, not same-setting improvements over v1. Phi-2 pruning ASR at 20% is inconsistently reported as 99.3% in Table 2 and 99.5% in Table 8.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1, 4.1, A.1, and A.2, Corollary 5.1, and their mathematical assumptions and proofs are retained. Appendix renumbering, incorporating the row-space remark into the theorem presentation, and a notation correction do not alter the mathematics. Section 7.4 describes an approximation procedure without adding a formal derivation or proved guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain stable. The conclusion narrows the practical defense claim: v1 says estimated Lipschitz constants can certify safe compression regimes, whereas v2 emphasizes robustness diagnostics based on sensitivity estimates. This qualifies practical applicability without replacing the central theoretical or backdoor claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses the restrictive single-layer setting and labels the new local approximation a sensitivity tool rather than a formal certificate. Section 7.3 also replaces the broad practical safety wording with a statement tied to the particular sample, estimated Lipschitz constant, and 10% pruning. Existing appendix limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly supplies a code-repository address and a reference to running instructions. Table 4 adds Phi-2 architecture and compression-location details, and Section 7.4 identifies autograd for the approximation. Existing hardware and software disclosures remain unchanged; Table 5 does not add Phi-2-specific loss constants.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.1 substantially develops the relationship to prior weight-perturbation research, contrasting Theorem 3.1 with Tsai et al. and Theorem 4.1 with Weng et al. Expanded Section 4 and Appendix B also position the work against input-space and parameter-space Lipschitz research, including newly cited Herrera, Bartlett, Fazlyab, Pauli, and Tsuzuku.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. Localized edits expand the applicability discussion, rewrite and rename the Summary as Conclusion, add an Impact Statement and related-work subsection, and update cross-references. These do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column conference formatting, substantially resizing and relocating displays and changing headers and typography. v2 adds Figure 4 and three Phi-2 result tables and expands the architecture table. The five original figures remain visually unchanged apart from placement and size.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 improves research positioning, qualifies practical certification claims, and supplies code-access information. The Phi-2 experiments and sensitivity analysis make applicability to modern language models more assessable. These gains are limited by incomplete Phi-2 settings, missing standard deviations despite captions promising them, and the conflicting pruning ASR in Tables 2 and 8. The revision provides a useful but imperfect extension of the retained work.
